look_here_first: Small fine-textured sedge with very narrow leaves and a compact cluster of several tiny spikes bearing spreading or reflexed perigynia.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Personal List; current Kew accepts the species as Texas-native.
project_inclusion.range_guardrail: Installed for active visual learning; exact target-zone county reconciliation is deferred and native metrics remain excluded.

morphology_keys.family_pattern: Cyperaceae/Carex: grasslike sedges with sheathing leaves; the fruit is enclosed in a perigynium, and perigynium shape/beak/venation are often decisive for species ID.
best_field_traits: green to pale-yellow perigynia with short beaks
dry to wet-mesic open forest and field habitat
morphology_keys.comparison_training: C. texensis is the smallest and finest-textured member of B105. Its narrow leaves and tiny clustered spikes contrast strongly with broad-leaved C. cherokeensis and the large winged fruits of C. tetrastachya.
